record.paper_title: Three open problems in function theoretic operator theory
record.original_question: Let A be a complex matrix whose numerical range W(A) is an elliptical disk, possibly degenerate. Does Crouzeix's inequality ||p(A)|| <= 2 max{|p(z)| : z is in W(A)} hold for every complex polynomial p?

evidence.quote: Question 2.7. Let A be a matrix with elliptical numerical range. Does Crouzeix's conjecture hold
This may be a good problem to consider next.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a square complex matrix $A \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$, let $\|A\|$ denote its operator norm (induced by the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb{C}^n$) and let
$$W(A) = \{\langle Ax, x\rangle : x \in \mathbb{C}^n,\ \|x\|=1\}$$
denote its numerical range. Crouzeix's inequality asserts that for every complex polynomial $p$,
$$\|p(A)\| \le 2\,\sup\{|p(z)| : z \in W(A)\}.$$
Suppose that $W(A)$ is an elliptical disk (i.e., the closed convex region bounded by an ellipse), allowing degenerate cases where the ellipse collapses to a line segment or a point. Does Crouzeix's inequality hold for every such matrix $A$ and every complex polynomial $p$?
artifact.status_search_result: Crouzeix's conjecture remains open in full generality (the best known constant is 1+√2 due to Crouzeix–Palencia, 2017). For matrices with elliptical numerical range, partial results are known: for example, the conjecture holds for all 3×3 tridiagonal matrices with constant main diagonal, equivalently 3×3 matrices whose numerical range is an ellipse centered at an eigenvalue (Glader–Kurula–Lindström, 2018). The general case of arbitrary matrices with elliptical numerical range does not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.snippet: holds for all tridiagonal 3×3 matrices with constant main diagonal... equivalent to 3×3 matrices with elliptic numerical range and one eigenvalue at the center of the ellipse
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture is verified for a subclass of matrices with elliptical numerical range; general elliptical case not stated as resolved.
